The deadweight loss is the area between the demand and supply curves from the after-tax quantity \(Q_t\) to the original equilibrium quantity \(Q_0\).  
The condition after tax is \( \text{demand price} - \text{supply price} = 850 \).  
At \(Q=0\), the difference is \(857-6=851\); at \(Q=10\), it is \(856-12=844\). Linear interpolation gives \(Q_t = 10/7\).  
The original equilibrium occurs where demand equals supply. From the data, at \(Q=1190\) the difference is \(7\), at \(Q=1200\) it is \(-3\); linear interpolation gives \(Q_0 = 1197\).  

The integral of the difference \(D(Q) = \text{demand} - \text{supply}\) from \(Q_t\) to \(Q_0\) is computed piecewise:  
- From \(Q_t\) to \(10\): width \(10 - 10/7 = 60/7\), average height \((850+844)/2 = 847\), area \(847 \cdot 60/7 = 7260\).  
- From \(10\) to \(1190\): sum over each 10‑unit interval using the trapezoid rule: \(\sum_{i=1}^{118} 5(D(10i)+D(10i+10)) = 493235\).  
- From \(1190\) to \(Q_0\): width \(7\), endpoints \(D(1190)=7\) and \(D(1197)=0\), area \(7\cdot7/2 = 49/2 = 24.5\).  

Total deadweight loss = \(7260 + 493235 + 24.5 = 500519.5 = \frac{1001039}{2}\).  

Thus the answer is \(\frac{1001039}{2}\).

ANSWER: 1001039/2
